description:
Securely validate webhooks, API signatures and incoming secret tokens right inside your Bubble workflows. Secret Validator provides a lightweight, server-side action designed to perform cryptographic validations — such as HMAC signatures or token verification — without ever exposing your sensitive keys or private credentials to the client. Keep your external integrations tight, secure and fully verified.

Key Features:
🔒 Secure Server-Side Validation: Processes your verification tokens exclusively on the server to prevent data leaks.

⚡ Ultra-Fast Execution: Highly optimised logic with zero unnecessary dependencies for lightning-fast workflow speeds.

✅ Simple Contract: Pass the incoming value, get a single is_valid boolean back, and branch your workflow on it.

🤝 Seamless Integration: Perfect for verifying webhooks from third-party platforms such as Stripe, GitHub, Shopify or your own APIs before processing the data.

🛡️ Fail Closed: Put it first in your backend workflow so unverified requests never reach the steps that write data.

Plugin support: https://inova.us/support
name: Secret Validator
plugin_instructions:
[b][size=5]Setup Instructions[/size][/b]

[b]Secret Validator[/b] allows you to securely verify incoming webhooks, API request signatures or secret tokens entirely on the server-side using a shared secret key.

[b][size=4]1. Add Your Secret Key[/size][/b]
Before using the action, you must provide your private secret (e.g. the webhook signing secret from GitHub or Shopify, or your own API token):
[list]
[*]Go to the [b]Plugins[/b] tab in your Bubble app settings.
[*]Locate [b]Secret Validator[/b].
[*]Enter your private key into the [b]Secret[/b] input field (make sure to set it for both development and production versions if applicable). [i]This keeps your key safely hidden on the server.[/i]
[/list]
If no Secret is set, the action always returns "no".

[b][size=4]2. Add the Action to your Workflow[/size][/b]
In your backend workflows (usually an API Workflow built to handle incoming webhooks), add the [b]Validate Secret[/b] server-side action as the very first step.

[b][size=4]3. Choose a Mode[/size][/b]
[b]Exact match[/b] (default): compares [b]Value[/b] with your Secret in constant time. Use this for static tokens sent in a header or query parameter.

[b]HMAC[/b]: computes an HMAC signature of [b]Payload[/b] with your Secret and compares it with the signature in [b]Value[/b]. Fields:
[list]
[*][b]Value:[/b] the signature header sent by the provider (e.g. X-Hub-Signature-256 or X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256).
[*][b]Payload:[/b] the exact content the provider signed, usually the raw request body. Re-serialised JSON will not match.
[*][b]Algorithm:[/b] SHA-256 (most providers), SHA-1 or SHA-512.
[*][b]Signature encoding:[/b] Hex or Base64.
[*][b]Signature prefix:[/b] optional text stripped from the start of Value, e.g. sha256=
[/list]
Examples:
[list]
[*][b]GitHub:[/b] Value = X-Hub-Signature-256 header, Algorithm = SHA-256, Encoding = Hex, Prefix = sha256=
[*][b]Shopify:[/b] Value = X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header, Algorithm = SHA-256, Encoding = Base64
[*][b]Stripe:[/b] from the Stripe-Signature header, set Value = the v1 signature and Payload = timestamp + "." + raw body; Algorithm = SHA-256, Encoding = Hex
[/list]

[b][size=4]4. Handle the Result[/size][/b]
The action returns a boolean [b]is_valid[/b].
[list]
[*]Add a [b]Conditional Decision (Only when...)[/b] to your subsequent workflow steps.
[*]Only allow your workflow to process data if the result of the validation step [b]is "yes"[/b].
[*]If the result is [b]"no"[/b], terminate the workflow or return a 401 Unauthorized response to block malicious requests.
[/list]
